title: The King's Chamber shafts end horizontally
summary: Geoffrey Drumm tells of The King's Chamber shafts end horizontally, about dynastic Egypt at Egypt (no place named), and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: The original archaeological documentation shows that the shafts go horizontal at the end.

plain: Inside the Great Pyramid at Giza in Egypt, a room called the King's Chamber has narrow shafts running out from it through the stone. A researcher named Geoffrey Drumm tells podcast host Jesse Michels that the original archaeological records show these shafts turn flat, running level, at their far ends. He brings it up as a clue in his own idea about what the pyramid was really built to do.
